name: How to Choose a Kitchen Overhauling Contractor for Older LA Homes and Current Codes

mainEntity.name: How do I choose a kitchen overhauling contractor in Los Angeles County who understands both older LA homes and current seismic and energy codes?
mainEntity.text: How do I choose a kitchen overhauling contractor in Los Angeles County who understands both older LA homes and current seismic and energy codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing a kitchen overhauling contractor in Los Angeles County for an older home requires more than just good design photos. Start by filtering for contractors who can show before‑and‑after projects in homes built before 1978 and who can explain how they handled knob‑and‑tube wiring, galvanized plumbing, and unreinforced framing. Ask directly how often they pull permits in your specific LA city and how they stay current with California Building Code, Title 24 energy rules, and local seismic requirements. A strong contractor will have structural engineers or design‑build teams they work with when removing or altering walls, adding large openings, or installing heavy islands and stone countertops. Request examples of recent projects where they upgraded electrical panels, added dedicated appliance circuits, and improved insulation and ventilation. Clarify who handles plan submittals, inspections, and responses to plan check comments. Finally, verify that their timeline and budget reflect the extra discovery work and potential surprises that come with older LA homes, and that their contract addresses change orders clearly so hidden structural or code issues do not spiral into uncontrolled costs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Look for a Los Angeles County kitchen overhauling contractor with specific experience in older LA housing stock and current California codes. Confirm they have projects in homes built before 1978, regularly pull permits in your city, coordinate with structural engineers when walls move, and can show recent work that upgraded electrical, plumbing, and insulation to meet Title 24 and seismic requirements.
